origin: Own exact low-fluence photophysical population model of anonymous chromophores. All optical signals are constructed noiseless oracle values, not measurements of a named material, molecule or device. The question is mechanism discrimination and excitation/photon accounting within a finite declared model family; it provides no synthesis, irradiation recipe or chemical engineering objective.
state_and_model_hypotheses: One absorbed photon prepares S(0)=1,P(0)=0,T(0)=0. S is a singlet excited population andP an intermediate population, both per initially absorbed photon. T counts FREE triplet excitations per initially absorbed photon; it is not automatically a probability. Consider exactly TWO candidate stoichiometries nu in{1,2}. Dynamics are Sdot=-(k_f+k_r+k_nr)*S+k_b*P; Pdot=k_f*S-(k_b+k_d+k_p)*P; Tdot=nu*k_d*P-k_t*T. All seven rate constants are finite and NONNEGATIVE, and k_f,k_b,k_d,k_t strictly positive. k_r is the singlet radiative rate, k_nr singlet nonradiative loss, k_p irreversible intermediate loss, k_d irreversible release EVENT rate, and k_b recycling back toS. A release event producesnu free triplets, never feeds S/P again, and each free triplet disappears independently at ratek_t. No other states, intensity-dependent annihilation, reabsorption, direct triplet formation, detector convolution or rate mixtures are allowed in these candidate models. After this pulse there is no additional excitation.
absolute_signal_calibration: The CSV gives the COMPLETE two observed time series at exact common times. FluorescenceF(t)=k_r*S(t) is an absolute photon flux per absorbed initial photon per time unit, with known unit detection efficiency; F(0) identifiesk_r becauseS(0)=1. The second calibrated signal is Y(t)=0.7*P(t)+0.2*T(t), with coefficients respectively per intermediate and per FREE triplet, not per triplet pair. Units and both positive response coefficients are fixed independently of the mechanism. Do not normalize signal amplitudes or infer a population by treating both coefficients as equal. Use every source row and both series.
global_identification: Determine EVERY nonnegative parameter solution for EACHnu candidate compatible with the complete source. Infer the full observed exponential-mode family rather than use one local nonlinear fit. ForY at equally spaced times, retain actual MatrixSVD of the full4x4HankelY_(i+j),i,j=0..3; actual appropriate linear/least-squares solution of EVERY order3recurrence row; and actual PolynomialRoots retaining all discrete decay roots before real/positive-domain selection. Fit all seven rows of BOTH signals to the complete common mode set with actual linear/least-squares tools and audit residuals. Missing/zero fluorescence amplitudes must be recognized as mode selection, not an invented zero measurement or discardedYmode. Audit lower order, repeated pole, missing mode and physically inadmissible root alternatives before asserting completeness. Rectangular systems require a suitable solver contract or a verified equivalent square realization.
mechanistic_reconstruction: Translate actual modes to positive continuous rates using the source time step. From normalizedS=F/F(0), and derivatives at0 implied by the complete fitted modal series, recover the2x2S/Pblock invariants and identify which pole is free-triplet loss. Infer k_f,k_b, k_r+k_nr, k_b+k_d+k_p and the PRODUCT nu*k_d from the calibrated derivatives. Then solve each candidate nu separately, retaining its requiredk_p even if negative. Do not repair a negative rate by clipping or silently changing optical cross sections. Give admittednuvalues, count of complete nonnegative solutions, all seven rates for the admitted model, and the k_p demanded by thenu=1candidate. Prove global uniqueness within this exact family, rather than confuse known-parameter observability with unknown-parameter identifiability.
observability_and_predictions: For the admitted model derive its full3x3column-state population generatorM and the2x3signal responseH=[[k_r,0,0],[0,0.7,0.2]]. Retain actual MatrixSVD ofH and of the full6x3observability stack[H;H*M;H*M^2]. Explain how a dynamically observable system can have fewer simultaneous signals than latent states. M evolves EXPECTED COUNTS and need not have column sums zero; do not force it to be a normalized3state Markov generator. Retain actual MatrixExponential of the COMPLETE M*t at each validation time[1,5,10]; propagate each returned matrix from the actual initial state and predict both latent populations and optical signals. Audit all frozen source times as well as these validation predictions.
events_vs_counts: Use actual MatrixInverse of minus the full transient2x2S/Pblock to compute its occupation integrals. From them report(i)probability of EVER enteringP,(ii)expected TOTAL number ofPformation events including recycling,(iii)eventualrelease-event probability,(iv)direct singlet loss and direct intermediate loss probabilities,(v)fluorescence photon quantum yield and singlet nonradiative loss probability,(vi)TOTAL free-triplet creation quantum yield and(vii)the time integral ofT. These quantities have different units and need not coincide. Prove conservation of all mutually exclusive eventual terminal fates. Repeated Pformation is not a distinct terminal event, and a free-triplet excitation count is not a single-event probability.
global_triplet_peak: Find the GLOBAL maximum ofT(t) for t>=0, its time and all three simultaneous populations. Retain actual MatrixExponential of the fullM at that inferred peak time, and propagate its actual returned matrix before reporting the peak. Prove that the positive stationary point is unique and global, including t=0and t->infinity, rather than take the largest sampled source value. You may derive the full exponential expression and analyze its derivative with a suitable monotonic/Rolle argument; an arbitrary numerical optimizer or grid is insufficient. Explain the difference between peak population, total production yield and eventual release probability.
energy_and_scope: Absorbed photon energy is exactly2.5eV; each CREATED free triplet carries1.0eV of electronic excitation energy in this model. Compute the fraction of absorbed photon energy represented by cumulative created-triplet energy. Radiative and other losses account for remaining channels; photon-number/exciton-number yield aboveone does not by itself imply energy creation. The nu=2interpretation is permitted by this energy budget; no energy extraction from an unspecified bath is needed for the stated accounting. A successful finite-class rate discrimination does not establish a unique unrestricted microscopic pathway in a real material.

interpretation_proposals.A: All three reported latent populations are probabilities whose unweighted sum must remain one.
interpretation_proposals.B: Absolute calibrated signal units are essential when distinguishing intermediate population from free-triplet excitation count.
interpretation_proposals.C: More than one triplet excitation per absorbed photon can be compatible with energy conservation.
interpretation_proposals.D: The free-triplet loss rate must be whichever singlet fluorescence pole decays fastest.
interpretation_proposals.E: Recycling can make expected intermediate formation count differ from the probability of ever forming that intermediate.
interpretation_proposals.F: A transient triplet-population maximum always equals the total triplet creation yield.
interpretation_proposals.G: Two instantaneous readouts can dynamically distinguish three latent coordinates when the full observability stack has sufficient rank.
interpretation_proposals.H: Rejecting one rate/stoichiometry candidate proves that no other microscopic photophysical mechanism could explain real measurements.

reporting: Use the public answer schema. Rate order[k_f,k_b,k_d,k_p,k_r,k_nr,k_t]; admittednuIDs are an unordered unique subset of{1,2}. Modal decay rates ascending. Latent arrays[S,P,T] and signal arrays[F,Y], validation times[1,5,10]. Probabilities and quantum yields are distinct: ONLY terminal/ever-event probabilities lie in[0,1]; T, its production yield and repeated event counts must not be artificially capped atone. Numeric tolerance1e-7absolute for rates, probabilities/populations/signals,1e-6for integrated populations and peak time. Exact ranks/counts/booleans/IDs; full derivations and actual receipts remain in the trajectory.
